topic: Jinbe and Ace fought for five days because Jinbe's loyalty goes to whoever protected his people
title: Jinbe And Ace Fought Five Days Over Whitebeard
description: Jinbe and Ace once fought for five straight days in chapter 552. Ace wanted Whitebeard's head, and Jinbe saw Whitebeard as the hero who protected Fish-Man Island. Here is why that duel explains so much about Jinbe.
comment: Who would have won the Jinbe and Ace fight if it had kept going: Jinbe or Ace?

lines.text: Jinbe fought Ace for five straight days over one man's life.

shot.fallback: fish-man fighting a fire fist pirate

lines.text: Ace wanted Whitebeard's head, and Jinbe saw Whitebeard as the hero who protected Fish-Man Island.

shot.fallback: giant old pirate captain over an underwater kingdom

lines.text: Neither could win, and both ended up too exhausted to stand. That's chapter 552.

shot.fallback: two fighters collapsed on a beach

lines.text: Jinbe was a Warlord of the Sea, and he still put Whitebeard before his own title.

shot.fallback: warlord in a kimono standing on a deck

lines.text: Later he refused to join the war against Whitebeard, even if it landed him in Impel Down. Chapter 523.

shot.fallback: huge prisoner sitting in a dark cell

lines.text: And here's the detail I love. Ace survived that duel, then fought Whitebeard right after it.

shot.fallback: fire fist pirate facing a giant captain

lines.text: That tells you what Jinbe's fists can do against a Logia user with Haki on his side.
The real rule with Jinbe is simple. He repays whoever protected his people, whatever it costs him.

shot.fallback: fish-man standing guard over his friends

lines.text: So what happens when that rule meets a captain who wants him aboard right now?

shot.fallback: rubber pirate captain offering his hand to a fish-man

lines.text: Because Jinbe fought Ace for five straight days over one man's life...
